speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I understand you are experiencing knee pain after recently increasing your physical activity; can you tell me exactly where on the knee the pain is located and whether it is sharp or dull?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient presents with knee pain that started yesterday and has been steadily worsening. She cites recent participation in volleyball involving repetitive pivoting and twisting movements as a possible cause. She was advised at her last physical exam that weight loss could be beneficial for her health.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your age, recent volleyball activity involving pivoting and twisting, and the location of the pain, is the swelling localized around the kneecap or is there a specific tender spot on the outer part of the knee? text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Insufficiency of the Medial Plica Syndrome.

The physical exam findings of tenderness medial to the patella, combined with your history of repetitive pivoting in volleyball and negative ligament stability tests, strongly suggest irritation of the medial plica rather than a meniscus or ligament tear.
